doc.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Cab's rhythm section, Mingus, marriage and the band's end
title: Missourians' dignity and studying bass with Zimmerman
summary: Hinton valued the Missourians' class and continued bass study; a Chicago teacher told him to study with Fred Zimmerman but not change his bow.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: He was the epitome. Cozy stayed there. He was energetic and he liked to study. That was a period of my life that I was very grateful to it, during all that Cab Calloway thing, for the Missourians. I‟m glad I got in when the Missourians was there because there‟s a lot of dignity to them, class. So I had no class. I didn‟t have any clothes or anything. I got a couple of dollars together so when… I‟m trying to get the class and dignity that these guys have. So when the band became a little raucous, I was the guy that was trying to hold up for the dignity. Then I was still concerned with really studying my bass. I found out… I‟d studied with Demetrius [Unintelligible], that‟s in Chicago, and he told me if I was coming to New York to study with Zimmerman but don‟t let him change my bow.
Yeah. Oscar was in Rochester. Oscar was done there.
Was Oscar on the faculty up there?
Yes, Oscar was on the faculty. Ron Carter studied with him.
Fred is the one that wrote the book though?
Yes, he was the one. Yeah, he‟s [unintelligible] with all those guys. Omar Mentz is the other one.
Phil [Unintelligible] is another big teacher from Detroit. I knew him too.
